name: Andrew Yang
subject: Welcome to my TED Talk
body:
| |
---
| | |
---
| [ ](https://yangspeaks.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7448319cdb745ea2fd1b1b8a8&id=4deb473085&e=0f227c2ae3)
---
|
Hello, I hope that your weekend was great.

I spent the past week at TED gearing up for my talk and delivering it – the topic was America’s political system, what is going wrong, and how we can improve it.
---
| [ ](https://yangspeaks.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7448319cdb745ea2fd1b1b8a8&id=f0c65c956d&e=0f227c2ae3)
---
|
For those of you who don’t know much about TED, it’s a conference that convenes a host of thinkers in technology, science and culture. The videos from people’s talks are widely circulated – it has 24 million subscribers on YouTube for example. A realistic expectation of the number of people who will wind up seeing this talk is probably 1 to 3 million, with a possibility of it being significantly higher - some talks get up to 6 million+ views.

I’ve spoken on America’s political system any number of times and feel very comfortable with the subject matter. But having a tailored talk with slides on a tight time frame still required some thought and work. The TED team asks that you rehearse and present to them multiple times in the run up to the conference. The venue holds about 1,700 people, and there’s one ‘take.’ So you definitely feel some pressure. Evelyn flew out to join me for the occasion – she’s never attended TED so it’s new to her.

The night before reminded me a little bit of a night before a presidential debate, where it’s tough to get to sleep. I woke up thinking, “Today’s the day!” I was eager to hit the message.

Backstage was restless. Scott Galloway was up after me, so we shared some time together. I heard my name called and bounded to the stage.

I’m glad to say the talk went great. The feedback was phenomenal. I got a standing ovation. People came up to me afterward to congratulate me. I definitely opened some eyes and minds to a different approach to the problems that ail us. One person said to me afterwards, “Thank you. I feel like the future of civilization may rest on whether your efforts succeed.” Others asked, “How can I help?” It felt awesome to deliver on what I knew was a big opportunity to get the word out.

**Why is this pledge important?** This election year, the influence of Big Oil looms large, with millions being funneled into disinformation campaigns and politicians who’ve sold out to the fossil fuel industry. As a result, the kind of action we need at every level of government is falling through the cracks. To keep our climate crisis from snowballing into climate catastrophe, we **need leaders who are unbound by the ties of oil money – true climate champions who:**
* **🌎 Refuse funding from fossil fuel companies, their executives, and lobbyists.**
* **🌎 Oppose the expansion of fossil fuel infrastructure and reject subsidies that support it.**

Friends,

I’m reaching out to you today because I’m running for Congress in Nevada’s 3rd District, **but I’m not what you might expect...**

You see, I’m not a lawyer, a politician, a bureaucrat, or even a big-time CEO.

_**I’m a composer.**_

_I created the soundtracks for a couple of large video game franchises you might have heard of – Halo and Destiny._

I know I’m the last person you might expect to run for office. But the truth is, I care too much about this country, and I can’t continue to stand by and let it head in the direction it’s going without jumping into the fight to save it.

Shortly after I launched my campaign last month, I was surprised and honored to receive this notification from **Elon Musk.**

[](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=669999388a344c7f87b5c66cdadd6023&_e=NF0_uvVhEHjd76czs9aNO_Yj7qD0BO6q_ko4ynAQC0F6Ydbnlz3t9oaB8GtqczU-xN1vlzuNbLBGKTXYhUc2Qy56UoXDQFaXBq-E2PdYu0uApDe6ea6qKavJ1tJ6uhMy3uvwmei_Zejob3jbHahIcAPGfoHy0neOpaXBlraXpUxSP_p7SzBBnD_OtjLQ09mpn2ENqVCVdE-oUhs6IeOqK3bdooUFKrs4gGGVhQuBO2Bkm4vaVtN_RQYu9_d6xUoFC6JvlM8VNXudR2lMqxYIJvEyXV7VC6X1uD7dhB76X9wIuQPtkxpFP4Olud4qemI6lqUKT7NBWIlOCYZYPUQLMdLP7iSEVHyaKbnEMqrMsODBhl2Kx3jYpPqkZB1CXlpXW-F4ch_XUjBcXJpkti8dSfhu0S8OEfQMCCRwQtvWX3k%3D)

Our tax-and-spend government continues to squeeze its citizens to the point that we’re just trying to survive, let alone thrive.

What we need is for our government to provide justice, safety, and freedom, and then _**get out of the way**_ and allow American families and businesses to grow and prosper.

| | | The Supreme Court will decide whether Trump has immunity from criminal prosecution for the crimes he committed while he was president. The Supreme Court must rule that Trump is not immune, and they must do it immediately. #
******REPUBLICAN DAVID FLIPPO ENDORSED BY LAST TWO PREVIOUS NV-04 NOMINEES**
---
| | **Las Vegas, NV** – Today former Assemblyman Jim Marchant and retired Air Force Major Sam Peters announced their endorsement of Lt.Col. David Flippo for Congress in Nevada’s 4th Congressional District (NV-04). Sam Peters was the Republican nominee for NV-04 in 2022, and Jim Marchant was the nominee in 2020.

Flippo commented on his endorsements:_

"I am honored to receive the endorsements of Jim and Sam, who came incredibly close to victory and understand the dynamics of our district intimately. Their support underscores our campaign's momentum and the growing consensus that it's time for committed, effective leadership. With their backing, we stand even stronger in our mission to advocate for smaller government and stronger leadership."_

| | Being outside has always been important to my family, Peter, and some of my earliest memories are floating down the Kishwaukee River. That, and kayaking, are traditions I continue today. [](http://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/JjLOWRdFKEAnBdrI9C_RUA~~/AAUS1gA~/RgRoCRuIP0TkaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYWN0Ymx1ZS5jb20vZG9uYXRlL2VzLXEyLTIwMjQ_) If you just listen to nature, you’ll learn a lot. As the foremost climate scientist in Congress, I can tell you that we need more messaging around this, and less about the “upcoming” global catastrophe. Because week-to-week, year-to-year, my time on the river makes it clear that the climate crisis is impacting our day-to-day lives _right now._ We’re paddling upriver on solving our climate crisis, and we owe it to our kids and grandkids to build a cleaner environment. It's my goal to frame climate change through the lens of how it impacts our daily lives. The ‘here and now’ can't be denied, and we need to paint that picture if we’re going to protect our homes, communities, and favorite pastimes from extreme weather events. [**I'm working to help end the climate crisis to give our children a livable world so they can have everlasting family memories of kayaking on the river, too. clean_body: Some of my earliest memories are floating down the Kishwaukee River. ~ | | Being outside has always been important to my family, Peter, and some of my earliest memories are floating down the Kishwaukee River. That, and kayaking, are traditions I continue today. If you just listen to nature, you’ll learn a lot. As the foremost climate scientist in Congress, I can tell you that we need more messaging around this, and less about the “upcoming” global catastrophe. Because week-to-week, year-to-year, my time on the river makes it clear that the climate crisis is impacting our day-to-day lives right now. We’re paddling upriver on solving our climate crisis, and we owe it to our kids and grandkids to build a cleaner environment. It's my goal to frame climate change through the lens of how it impacts our daily lives. The ‘here and now’ can't be denied, and we need to paint that picture if we’re going to protect our homes, communities, and favorite pastimes from extreme weather events. name: Gretchen Whitmer
subject: Earth Day
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Fight Like Hell PAC**
body:
Let’s fight like hell to protect our planet. |
#
---
Team — there’s no better day to take action to protect our climate than Earth Day. From the Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore to Tahquamenon Falls, Michigan is home to some of the most beautiful natural wonders found _anywhere_ in the world. We also hold 21% of the world’s freshwater and millions of acres of forest, lake shores, and farmland. **But as scientists continue to warn us of the costs of inaction, we must do more to protect our natural resources and landmarks by attacking the climate crisis head-on.** In Michigan, that’s _exactly_ what we’ve done. Seeing Gore wage a courageous and sometimes lonely struggle for action on the climate crisis taught me to never back down from what’s right when there’s a need for real change. I spent a decade starting and leading an environmentally-focused alternative to the Big Banks that put climate change fighting power into people's hands. We helped millions of Americans move billions of dollars of their savings deposits and personal investments out of the reach of Big Oil companies and into accounts that were fossil fuel-free. And we funded the planting of over one hundred million trees around the world to suck carbon dioxide out of the atmosphere. This isn’t some abstract or global issue for us here in Arizona. We’re facing the climate crisis right here and right now. Wildfires, drought, and deadly heat waves have become all too common. **There is no place in America where the climate crisis is a more clear and present danger than in Arizona. But Arizona should also be the “Solar State.” We can be to clean energy jobs what Detroit is to cars and Silicon Valley is to computers.** With the right leadership and vision in Washington, combating the climate crisis can be an enormous source of economic opportunity for Arizona. subject: Basically every big issue we work on, including climate change, comes down to this.

body:
Can I tell you a quick story?

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2137%2E4032634%2EDfovDH)
---
There are plenty of ways to celebrate Earth Day today. You could plant a tree, or help clean up a local park, or ride your bike instead of driving your car — all terrific. I want to make a pitch for one more step: taking political action to demand policy change. Because when we raise our voices side by side, over time, we make change happen — to ensure clean air, clean water, and a livable planet for our kids and grandkids. Can I tell you a quick story to try to make that case? It starts with how corporations — including many large players in the oil and gas industries — gamed the tax code, and ends with fighting climate change. (Yep — basically every big issue we work on comes down to tax policy.) You see, for years, giant corporations were raking in massive profits while paying little or no federal income taxes. In fact, during the period of 2018–2022, the largest profitable corporations in the oil, gas, and pipelines industry were paying an effective tax rate of only 2%. That just isn’t right. So I proposed a minimum tax on massive profits for billionaire corporations. People said it would never happen. They said corporate lobbyists had too much power. But this grassroots movement got behind the plan. I kept persisting in Washington. And in 2022, we got it passed — to help fund our nation’s biggest-ever investment in fighting the climate crisis. That tax is now powering clean energy innovation, new jobs, climate resiliency, environmental justice investments, and electric vehicle purchases across the country. Earth Day: A Celebration of Life and a Call to Action
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/earthdaydb [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/earthdaydb]
My GOP opponent Rep. Jack Bergman has been positioning for years to defund environmental protections and conservation efforts with drastic cuts. Help me defeat the Republican majority so we can halt their assault on environmental protections. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/earthdaydb]
CONTRIBUTE TO OUR EFFORTS [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/earthdaydb]
Friends,
Our district is blessed to be surrounded by three great lakes, which not only provide us with breathtaking views but also sustain our way of life. However, we cannot ignore the stark reality that our lakes and waters are under threat due to the effects of climate change.
As a congressional candidate for this region, I stand firmly supporting sustainable agricultural, mining, and logging practices. These industries play a vital role in our local economy, providing jobs and livelihoods for many. However, we must also recognize the importance of balancing economic growth with environmental responsibility.
While most believe in the necessity of conservation and funding to support our environmental protection agencies, Representative Bergman has proposed only cuts. This is not only short-sighted but also detrimental to the long-term health and sustainability of our natural resources.
Earth Day is not just a one-day celebration for us Yoopers and Northern Michiganders. It is a reminder that every day , we have a responsibility to be stewards of the land and water that have been entrusted to us . It is a call to action to preserve and protect our environment for future generations.
Today, as we come together to celebrate Earth Day, let us also engage in acts of service. Whether it is participating in a beach cleanup, planting trees, or advocating for stronger environmental policies, we can all contribute to the betterment of our planet.
Let us remember that our actions today will shape the world we leave behind for our children and grandchildren.
Let's create a legacy of environmental stewardship that will be remembered for generations to come.
Have a great Earth Day,
Onward,
-Bob

** FBI Raids Dolton Village Hall, Issues Subpoenas as Corruption Allegations Surround “Dolton Dictator” Mayor Tiffany Henyard (https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2024/04/fbi-raids-dolton-village-hall-issues-subpoenas-as-corruption-allegations-surround-dolton-dictator-mayor-tiffany-henyard.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=10d2419f58-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D)
------------------------------------------------------------

By Illinois Review

Last Friday, FBI agents made a surprise visit to Dolton Village Hall – a small suburb south of Chicago, and issued subpoenas – as Democrat Mayor Tiffany Henyard – dubbed the “worst mayor in America” faces numerous allegations of political corruption, silencing a sexual assault victim and misusing public funds.

On April 16th, Henyard’s top aide Keith Freeman, was charged with bankruptcy fraud and making false statements to hide financial information, including his sources of income in a bankruptcy petition. Freeman is a senior administrator in Dolton and Thornton Township. Henyard is both mayor of Dolton and the Thornton Township supervisor.
CLICK TO READ FULL ARTICLE (https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2024/04/fbi-raids-dolton-village-hall-issues-subpoenas-as-corruption-allegations-surround-dolton-dictator-mayor-tiffany-henyard.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=10d2419f58-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D)

Henyard remains in the headlines amid allegations of misusing public funds to fund an extravagant lifestyle. While Dolton – a small village in Cook County with a population of 21,000, has a medium household income of $54,000 – Henyard makes nearly $300,000 per year as village mayor and township supervisor. The mayor-supervisor also flies first class and stays at luxury hotels while on “official” business trips. Henyard is also surrounded by police officers that make up her own personal security detail even when she is out of state – and back home, she is driven around in a presidential-style motorcade that has cost local taxpayers more than $1 million. Henyard even uses a gold encrusted microphone while speaking at village hall. And while the mayor-supervisor spends taxpayer dollars to fund her lavish lifestyle, local vendors are not being paid and the village and residents continue to struggle financially.

FBI Raids Dolton Village Hall, Issues Subpoenas as Corruption Allegations Surround “Dolton Dictator” Mayor Tiffany Henyard () By Illinois Review Last Friday, FBI agents made a surprise visit to Dolton Village Hall – a small suburb south of Chicago, and issued subpoenas – as Democrat Mayor Tiffany Henyard – dubbed the “worst mayor in America” faces numerous allegations of political corruption, silencing a sexual assault victim and misusing public funds. On April 16th, Henyard’s top aide Keith Freeman, was charged with bankruptcy fraud and making false statements to hide financial information, including his sources of income in a bankruptcy petition. Freeman is a senior administrator in Dolton and Thornton Township. Henyard is both mayor of Dolton and the Thornton Township supervisor. CLICK TO READ FULL ARTICLE () Henyard remains in the headlines amid allegations of misusing public funds to fund an extravagant lifestyle. While Dolton – a small village in Cook County with a population of 21,000, has a medium household income of $54,000 – Henyard makes nearly $300,000 per year as village mayor and township supervisor. The mayor-supervisor also flies first class and stays at luxury hotels while on “official” business trips. Henyard is also surrounded by police officers that make up her own personal security detail even when she is out of state – and back home, she is driven around in a presidential-style motorcade that has cost local taxpayers more than $1 million. Henyard even uses a gold encrusted microphone while speaking at village hall. And while the mayor-supervisor spends taxpayer dollars to fund her lavish lifestyle, local vendors are not being paid and the village and residents continue to struggle financially. We just kicked off our campaign road trip, Peter, and what’s a road trip without some car tunes?
Naturally I requested Springsteen, one of my favorites. As I was listening to some of his greatest hits on the road, one lyric in particular stood out to me.
**“You can’t start a fire without a spark.”**
I believe this quote embodies the spirit of the campaign we’re running.
Our victory in November will be a fire. Protecting this seat will allow us to hold onto our Senate majority and continue fighting for Pennsylvanians, but we can’t do it without the spark of each individual supporter.
Whether it’s telling a friend about our campaign, wearing one of our t-shirts, or chipping in when you can, you are lighting a spark that helps power this re-election campaign, and I couldn’t be more grateful.

As you probably already know, last year we bought a former **nightclub** in Tulsa and transformed it into a **church** that is uniquely [Sheridan.Church](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=9380132.4202.1.361d811f3d92cf2cb0206e34da4d0ba9). The process of taking a **tavern** and turning it into a **tabernacle** was amazing. We have decided to make a difference in the education sphere due to the _wild + woke indoctrination_ that is taking place around us with our children. In the Fall of 2024 we will be opening up a **Learning Center** at [Sheridan.Church](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=9380132.4203.1.4ab5de99b4560a7de40a881fde057a04). This will include a _Daycare_ , _Preschool_ & _Kindergarten_. My wife, Kendra, has a background in Education with her Bachelors + Masters being in Education and she will lead the Learning Center. To launch this in the Fall we need to **build 3 more classrooms** over the spring and summer as well as adding a **playground**. This is going to cost around $30,000 to accomplish. This email is going out to over 250,000 great Americans. If just 1000 of the 250,000 would give $30 then we would meet our goal instantly. Please consider partnering with us to make this dream a reality. Every person that makes a donation of any size towards the Learning Center will be entered into a drawing this week to win a trip for 2 on a cruise. You can give at [www.sheridan.church/give](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=9380132.4204.1.b33fcb3d11447a8bcc901728c174b2b0) Thank you,
Pastor Jackson Lahmeyer

subject: As Baugh Takes NRA Money, Min Stands with Law Enforcement
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/4cb5eff69966/as-baugh-takes-nra-money-min-stands-with-law-enforcement-16195483?e=7017cc100e)

| |

| | **For Immediate Release** : April 22, 2023
**Contact** : press@davemin.com
**As Baugh Takes NRA Money, Min Stands with Law Enforcement**
**IRVINE, CA** — Amid a dismal fundraising quarter, Republican Scott Baugh has turned to the gun lobby, accepting thousands in campaign donations as he struggles to gain financial traction following the loss of Californian Kevin McCarthy as Speaker of the House. During the first quarter of 2024, Baugh solicited funds from both the NRA Victory Fund and the National Shooting Sports Foundation PAC– two organizations known for the relentless opposition to gun control measures and significant role in perpetuating the gun violence crisis. This comes in stark contrast to his Democratic opponent, State Senator Dave Min, who has positioned himself as a leading advocate for sensible gun control measures and the is only candidate endorsed by police officers.

>From the outset of his tenure, State Senator Dave Min has been a key figure in California's battle against gun violence, initiating Senate Bill (SB) 264 to eliminate gun shows at the Orange County Fairgrounds and pioneering SB 915 in 2022 to prohibit the sale of firearms and ammunition on all state property—a first in the nation. He further cemented his leadership in gun safety by partnering with the Brady Campaign on SB 1384, requiring firearms dealers to carry liability insurance and install onsite surveillance. Dave's staunch opposition to the gun lobby is underscored by his 'F' rating from the NRA, a badge of honor reflecting his unwavering commitment to safeguarding Californians against gun violence. In addition to his efforts to combat gun violence, Dave is the only candidate in the race for CA-47 endorsed by police officers, including the [Peace Officers Research Association of California (PORAC)](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=d1325d1ea6&e=7017cc100e), the state’s largest police union and the largest statewide association of police officers in the country, [Los Angeles Police Protective League (LAPPL)](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=d5550784b6&e=7017cc100e), [Association of Los Angeles Deputy Sheriffs (ALADS)](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=309cffa399&e=7017cc100e) and [The California Lodge of the Fraternal Order of Police](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=2917c8dc69&e=7017cc100e). During his time in the State Senate, Dave worked closely with local law enforcement to combat rising crime and homelessness, including authoring two key bills to address rider safety on public transit, and procuring $1 million for local police to help keep our communities safe.

The differences between Min and Baugh could not be starker. While Scott Baugh began his career as a corrupt State Assemblymember, engaging in campaign finance fraud, perjury, and obstruction of justice, which led to his being indicted for 22 criminal charges (including 4 felony counts), Dave Min began his career cracking down on corporate fraud and corruption as an SEC prosecutor. While Baugh has embraced whackjob conspiracy theories associated with white nationalism, stating that “wokeness” was a more dangerous threat to America’s security than 9/11 or World War II, Min has repeatedly celebrated diversity and stood up against hate in Orange County. And while Baugh has made clear that he would support a total abortion ban, without exceptions, even in the case of rape, incest, or danger to a woman’s life, Min has earned a 100% rating from Planned Parenthood and authored eight leading domestic violence bills into law.
###

California’s 47th is an open Congressional District in Orange County that includes the Cities of Costa Mesa, Huntington Beach, Irvine, Newport Beach, and Seal Beach, and portions of Laguna Beach, Laguna Hills, and Laguna Woods. Incumbent Katie Porter is vacating the seat to run for U.S. Senate. In 2022, Porter defeated former Assemblymember Republican Scott Baugh by 3.44% in this “toss-up” district. State Senator Dave Min currently represents over 80% of Congressional District 47 in Sacramento. In 2020, Min received over 158,000 votes within CA-47, defeating incumbent John Moorlach by 5.15% in this area. 19% of the registered voters in CA-47 are of Asian and Pacific Islander descent, including one of the largest Korean-American populations in the country.

**About Jim Jordan:** Leading the fight to hold Washington accountable.

**
In Washington, Jim Jordan is focused on his oversight role, helping lead investigations into federal agencies

In Congress, Jim Jordan continued to fight for fiscal responsibility,and he offered the only balanced budget of any member of the House or Senate.

As a state legislator, he took on the powerful special interests and the leaders from both political parties who wanted to put Ohio on an unsustainable path of higher taxes and spending.

Dear Peter,
If we want to meet our obligation as a generation, as a civilization, as a nation, we must create communities for our children that offer the same opportunities for dignity, enrichment, prosperity, and good health as the communities our parents provided for us.
To achieve this, we must begin by protecting our environment: the air we breathe, the water we drink, the wildlife, the fisheries, and the public lands.
These are not mere properties but belong to all of us—the commons, the commonwealth, the landscapes, and waterways that connect us to the 10,000 generations before the era of laptops, and ultimately to God.
God communicates with human beings through many vectors: through each other, organized religion, the great books of those religions, wise people, art, music, literature, and poetry. Yet, He does so nowhere with such detail, grace, color, and joy as through creation.
When we destroy a species or a special place, _we diminish our capacity to sense the divine_ , to understand who God is, and what our own potential is as human beings.
I believe we deserve a President who cares deeply about these issues and discusses them openly with the American people.
I am committed to preserving our environmental heritage for future generations and need your support to make this vision a reality. [Join our cause and help ensure that our children can inherit a world as rich and promising as the one we were given.](https://www.kennedy24.com/nature-video-donate?e=d33e868971601c1c714cfe0555abd394&utm_source=joinkennedy&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=earth_day_message_4_22_24_a4&n=5)
Thank you for your faithful support!

Sincerely,
Robert F. Kennedy, Jr.

To achieve this, we must begin by protecting our environment: the air we breathe, the water we drink, the wildlife, the fisheries, and the public lands. These are not mere properties but belong to all of us—the commons, the commonwealth, the landscapes, and waterways that connect us to the 10,000 generations before the era of laptops, and ultimately to God. God communicates with human beings through many vectors: through each other, organized religion, the great books of those religions, wise people, art, music, literature, and poetry. Yet, He does so nowhere with such detail, grace, color, and joy as through creation. When we destroy a species or a special place, we diminish our capacity to sense the divine , to understand who God is, and what our own potential is as human beings. I believe we deserve a President who cares deeply about these issues and discusses them openly with the American people. I am committed to preserving our environmental heritage for future generations and need your support to make this vision a reality. Thank you for your faithful support! | | Sincerely, Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. P.S. , where Nicole Shanahan and I will share our vision for healthy people and a healthy planet. | | | PAID FOR BY TEAM KENNEDY Would you like help donating? subject: This week in Texas - April 22

body:
[1]Powered By People

Here’s what Powered by People is working on this week:

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Early voting for May 4 elections begins today

There are local elections across the state that include bond propositions,
state senate contests and election for property appraisal district boards.
Early voting begins today.

You can learn more about the elections in your area by entering your
address in this guide provided by Texas Tribune:
[ https://act.betoorourke.com/go/63420?t=1001&akid=239562%2E444211%2EiuysY9 ]texastribune.org/2024/04/17/texas-local-elections-voting-may-2024/

Courage on campus

I spent last Tuesday on the University of Texas campus helping to register
students to vote.

I was impressed by the number of young people we registered and even more
so by the things they were telling me. Many described how eager they are
to change our country and state for the better and told me how they chose
their field of study (medicine, engineering, philosophy and business just
to name four that came up) to do just that.

What surprised me was how often I was asked about SB 17, the legislation
that has outlawed Texas public universities’ attempts to improve
diversity, equity and inclusion on their campuses. Students expressed
concern with the impact it was having on UT’s ability to attract and
retain the talent necessary for it to continue to be a leading university.
They talked about the firing of staff and the disbanding of committees and
working groups that were important in the work they have been pursuing.

UT President Jay Hartzell recently told faculty that “we need to not only
comply with the law, but also act in ways that restore and raise public
confidence.” A pernicious quality of authoritarian regimes is the bowing
and scraping performed by those who wish to curry favor with the "dear
leader." Or who just want to keep their jobs. In this case, it appears
University leadership went far beyond mere compliance in order to
anticipate the wishes of the law’s supporters, people like State Sen.
Brandon Creighton, Lieutenant Governor Dan Patrick and Governor Abbott.

One of the students asked me how we can change this. My answer: we must
replace those who voted for laws like SB17 by voting them out of office.
That’s why Powered by People is on this campus and campuses across Texas,
registering and staying in touch with the voters who have the power to
change this state for the better.

[ https://act.betoorourke.com/go/63421?t=1002&akid=239562%2E444211%2EiuysY9 ]If you live in Texas, you can help us by becoming a Volunteer Deputy
Registrar (VDR). Sign up for a short, virtual VDR training with us this
week and then we’ll put you to work on a college campus near you.

SIGN UP FOR A VDR TRAINING

[ https://act.betoorourke.com/signup/texting-team/?source=em20240422&t=1003&akid=239562%2E444211%2EiuysY9 ]If you live out of state, you can help with this effort by joining our
Texting Team. Sign up here and then we’ll reach out soon with instructions
on how you can join our text banks to help Texans register to vote.

JOIN OUR TEXTING TEAM

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

I hope it’s a great week for you.

— Beto

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way for us to reach you about opportunities to act. If you need to remove yourself from our email list, click here to unsubscribe: https://act.betoorourke.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=1004&akid=239562%2E444211%2EiuysY9

PAID FOR BY POWERED BY PEOPLE

clean_body: Happy Earth Day, friends! 🌎 | | | Peter, when you think of Earth Day, our veterans probably aren’t the first thing to come to mind. But during my time as USDA’s Military Veterans Agricultural Liaison, and as a veteran myself, I saw that transitioning from the military to a life in agriculture became a natural fit for many. And when I served the Department, I helped implement policies to support veterans starting farms or ranches of their own. Protecting our planet and investing in climate solutions is just plain common-sense at this point. But what most folks don’t recognize is that providing a safe, sustainable outlet for our retired service members through agriculture is key to supporting our veterans and their re-entry into civilian life. | Folks, there are currently over 84,900 Iowa farming businesses operating over 30 million acres across our state. Protecting our planet isn’t just a talking point — it’s key to ensuring one of Iowa’s top business industries remains sustainable for generations to come. The truth is that when we put our planet first, everyone wins — from our veterans-turned-farmers, to our small businesses, to everyday Iowans shopping at the grocery store. Thanks for reading, Peter! I hope you get the chance to step outside and enjoy our beautiful Earth today! 🌎 — Lanon | = | ---|--- Lanon Baccam is a veteran, a lifelong Iowan, and now, he's running to restore principled, effective leadership in Washington. right now to help Summer defeat her GOP billionaire-backed opponent?

Squad Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, local elected officials, and labor leaders
— together, they fired up voters and made it clear: this House seat isn’t
for sale.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jdem-pts-email-sl.wJpHnY&refcode=em20240422-34434&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=34434%2E1203867%2EtYIWIl ]Tweet from @joanegreve: AOC takes the stage in Pittsburgh to rally for

but by a lot.” Photo of rally.

to the one percent,” as a young, Black, progressive incumbent is
challenged by a so-called Democrat backed by Jeff Yass, an anti-abortion,
anti-public education billionaire who’s donated more to the GOP this year
than anyone else in the country.

“On Tuesday what we must do is show [Summer] and show the world and show
the people in that big White House that she is not alone. It’s not about
winning, it’s about winning big.” — AOC

Summer was underestimated when she first ran for this seat in 2022, but
through this people-powered movement, she overcame millions in attacks
from right-wing groups like AIPAC and Moderate PAC and won. Now, we need
to help her do it again tomorrow.

Hi folks, Tammy Baldwin here with an important update:
**A brand new poll shows that my Senate race in Wisconsin is TIED 50-50.**
My megamillionaire Republican opponent is gaining ground in Wisconsin -- _and fast._
First, he plastered Wisconsin’s airwaves with more than $4 million worth of ads. Then, the Republican primary field cleared for Hovde, giving him more than 7 uninterrupted months to campaign against me. **Now, the latest polling has us tied.**
Republicans are going all in to flip this seat red, and we can’t expect him to let up. Eric Hovde has pledged to self-fund at least $20 million of his own personal fortune to defeat me, _and he’s on pace to spend even more than that._
Look, unlike my wealthy opponent, I can’t self-fund this campaign. I don’t have right-wing dark money groups or GOP megadonors who can spend a fortune to tilt the scales in my favor.
Instead, I’m counting on grassroots supporters like you to help me fight back. We need your help to reach undecided voters, keep our ads on the air, and make sure Hovde’s attacks don’t go unanswered.

body:
| | | [](greattask.com)
---
| | Peter, Thank you for following Liz's efforts with Our Great Task. We wanted to share her op-ed in the New York Times this morning. [In her op-ed,](https://link.quorum.us/f/a/dqqDAn2qR33qpuxVI1l8cQ~~/AACYXwA~/RgRoCToTP0RMaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubnl0aW1lcy5jb20vMjAyNC8wNC8yMi9vcGluaW9uL3RydW1wLWltbXVuaXR5LXN1cHJlbWUtY291cnQuaHRtbFcDc3BjQgpmEDe1JmaN63KBUhRkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbVgEAAAAAA~~) she urges the U.S. Supreme Court to rule quickly AND to "fashion its decision in a way that does not lead to further time-consuming appeals on presidential immunity." Americans deserve to hear the federal case so they have a full understanding of Trump's actions leading up to and on Jan. 6 before they vote in November. See the full piece below and [tune in on Wednesday night at 7pm ET](https://link.quorum.us/f/a/Hc4BJ8Wl4ROp10elNSYFYw~~/AACYXwA~/RgRoCToTP0RXaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYy1zcGFuLm9yZy92aWRlby8_NTM0OTUxLTEvZm1yLXJlcC1saXotY2hlbmV5LXItd3ktY29udmVyc2F0aW9uLWpvbi1tZWFjaGFtVwNzcGNCCmYQN7UmZo3rcoFSFGRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tWAQAAAAA) when she discusses this and more [with Jon Meachem at the National Cathedral in Washington, DC](https://link.quorum.us/f/a/2sDM5LHmDu9j8zkxfoIhMg~~/AACYXwA~/RgRoCToTP0ReaHR0cHM6Ly9jYXRoZWRyYWwub3JnL2NhbGVuZGFyL3ByaW5jaXBsZXMtcG9saXRpY3MtYW4tZXZlbmluZy13aXRoLWxpei1jaGVuZXktYW5kLWpvbi1tZWFjaGFtL1cDc3BjQgpmEDe1JmaN63KBUhRkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbVgEAAAAAA~~): **[ _NYT:_(Cheney) The Supreme Court Should Rule Swiftly On Trump’s Immunity Claim](https://link.quorum.us/f/a/dqqDAn2qR33qpuxVI1l8cQ~~/AACYXwA~/RgRoCToTP0RMaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubnl0aW1lcy5jb20vMjAyNC8wNC8yMi9vcGluaW9uL3RydW1wLWltbXVuaXR5LXN1cHJlbWUtY291cnQuaHRtbFcDc3BjQgpmEDe1JmaN63KBUhRkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbVgEAAAAAA~~)**April 22, 2024 _On Thursday, the U.S. Supreme Court will hear Donald Trump’s arguments that he is immune from prosecution for his efforts to steal the 2020 presidential election. It is likely that all — or nearly all — of the justices agree that a former president who attempted to seize power and remain in office illegally can be prosecuted. I suspect that some justices may also wish to clarify whether doctrines of presidential immunity might apply in other contexts — for example, to a president’s actions as commander in chief during a time of war. But the justices should also recognize the profoundly negative impact they may have if the court does not resolve these issues quickly and decisively.

**If delay prevents this Trump case from being tried this year, the public may never hear critical and historic evidence developed before the grand jury, and our system may never hold the man most responsible for Jan. 6 to account.
**
The Jan. 6 House select committee’s hearings and final report in 2022 relied on testimony given by dozens of Republicans — including many who worked closely with Mr. Trump in the White House, in his Justice Department and on his 2020 presidential campaign. Special counsel Jack Smith’s election-related indictment of Mr. Trump relies on many of the same firsthand witnesses. Although the special counsel reached a number of the same conclusions as the select committee, the indictment is predicated on a separate and independent investigation. Evidence was developed and presented to a grand jury sitting in Washington, D.C.

**The indictment and public reporting suggest that the special counsel was able to obtain key evidence our committee did not have.** For example, it appears that the grand jury received evidence from witnesses such as Mark Meadows, the former Trump chief of staff, and Dan Scavino, a former Trump aide, both of whom refused to testify in our investigation. Public reporting also suggests that members of Mr. Trump’s Office of White House Counsel and other White House aides testified in full, without any limitations based on executive privilege, as did Vice President Mike Pence and his counsel.

The special counsel’s indictment lays out Mr. Trump’s detailed plan to overturn the 2020 election, including the corrupt use of fraudulent slates of electors in several states. According to the indictment, senior advisers in the White House, Justice Department and elsewhere repeatedly warned that Mr. Trump’s claims of election fraud were false and that his plans for Jan. 6 were illegal. Mr. Trump chose to ignore those warnings. (Remember what the White House lawyer Eric Herschmann told Mr. Trump’s alleged co-conspirator John Eastman on Jan. 7, 2021: “Get a great f’ing criminal defense lawyer. You’re gonna need it.”) **There is little doubt that Mr. Trump’s closest advisers also gave the federal grand jury minute-to-minute accounts of his malicious conduct on Jan. 6, describing how they repeatedly begged the president to instruct the violent rioters to leave our Capitol and how Mr. Trump refused for several hours to do so as he watched the attack on television**.**This historic testimony about a former president’s conduct is likely to remain secret until the special counsel presents his case at trial.**

**As a criminal defendant, Mr. Trump has long had access to federal grand jury material relating to his Jan. 6 indictment and to all the testimony obtained by our select committee. He knows what all these witnesses have said under oath and understands the risks he faces at trial. That’s why he is doing everything possible to try to delay his Jan. 6 federal criminal trial until after the November election.** If the trial is delayed past this fall and Mr. Trump wins re-election, he will surely fire the special counsel, order his Justice Department to drop all Jan. 6 cases and try to prevent key grand jury testimony from ever seeing the light of day.

I know how Mr. Trump’s delay tactics work. Our committee had to spend months litigating his privilege claims (in Trump v. Thompson) before we could gain access to White House records. Court records and public reporting suggest that the special counsel also invested considerable time defeating Mr. Trump’s claims of executive privilege, which were aimed at preventing key evidence from reaching the grand jury. **All of this evidence should be presented in open court, so that the public can fully assess what Mr. Trump did on Jan. 6 and what a man capable of that type of depravity could do if again handed the awesome power of the presidency.**

Early this year, a federal appeals court took less than a month after oral argument to issue its lengthy opinion on immunity. **History shows that the Supreme Court can act just as quickly, when necessary.** And the court should fashion its decision in a way that does not lead to further time-consuming appeals on presidential immunity. It cannot be that a president of the United States can attempt to steal an election and seize power but our justice system is incapable of bringing him to trial before the next election four years later.

Mr. Trump believes he can threaten and intimidate judges and their families, assert baseless legal defenses and thereby avoid accountability altogether. Through this conduct, he seeks to break our institutions. If Mr. Trump’s tactics prevent his Jan. 6 trial from proceeding in the ordinary course, he will also have succeeded in concealing critical evidence from the American people — evidence demonstrating his disregard for the rule of law, his cruelty on Jan. 6 and the deep flaws in character that make him unfit to serve as president. The Supreme Court should understand this reality and conclude without delay that no immunity applies here.
_ [Full Essay Here](https://link.quorum.us/f/a/dqqDAn2qR33qpuxVI1l8cQ~~/AACYXwA~/RgRoCToTP0RMaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubnl0aW1lcy5jb20vMjAyNC8wNC8yMi9vcGluaW9uL3RydW1wLWltbXVuaXR5LXN1cHJlbWUtY291cnQuaHRtbFcDc3BjQgpmEDe1JmaN63KBUhRkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbVgEAAAAAA~~) Thanks, Kara

body:
First graders in the 7th District are being taught about pronouns | | | [](https://a1e0.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=6626b40fd59aea161b0f8090&u=https%3A%2F%2Ftombarrettforcongress.com%2F%3Fss_source%3Dsscampaigns%26ss_campaign_id%3D66269bffc16c0c394cf826d3%26ss_email_id%3D6626b40fd59aea161b0f8090%26ss_campaign_name%3DCan%25E2%2580%2599t%2Bwe%2Bjust%2Blet%2Bkids%2Bbe%2Bkids%253F%26ss_campaign_sent_date%3D2024-04-22T19%253A06%253A24Z&w=618846223a022e7ecb41d30c&c=b_66269bffc16c0c394cf826d3&l=en-US&s=CIZnzN6kW4z5ziWAz_IiGDsuHTo%3D)
---
| Can’t we just let kids be kids?Peter Willis, we are raising four small children, including a first grader, so we can’t tell you how disappointed we were to learn last week that [**an elementary school not far from our house decided to teach first graders how to “share and explore pronouns.”**](https://a1e0.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=6626b40fd59aea161b0f8090&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.dropbox.com%2Fscl%2Ffi%2Fb3d9v3swnqf6pcjlw7kym%2FSchavey-Road-Letter.jpg%3Fdl%3D0%26rlkey%3D4wbcen9mjgkbi609bko63ojpf&w=618846223a022e7ecb41d30c&c=b_66269bffc16c0c394cf826d3&l=en-US&s=45219majSsMEA4xMTb5gKBb0Rf8%3D)
---
| [](https://a1e0.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=6626b40fd59aea161b0f8090&u=https%3A%2F%2Fnypost.com%2F2024%2F04%2F19%2Fus-news%2Fwoke-school-district-doubles-down-on-teaching-students-about-new-gender-pronouns-including-the-phrase-tree%2F&w=618846223a022e7ecb41d30c&c=b_66269bffc16c0c394cf826d3&l=en-US&s=GUMFt2rhy_7SbPVEB6L2k3ADe_c%3D)
---
_**These kids are first graders.**_
---
[_ _ Donate _ _](https://a1e0.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=6626b40fd59aea161b0f8090&u=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.winred.com%2Ftom-barrett-for-congress%2Flet-kids-be-kids&w=618846223a022e7ecb41d30c&c=b_66269bffc16c0c394cf826d3&l=en-US&s=0nEODOujPJ20P6zKk7BIT1DCgps%3D)
---
It’s already incredibly difficult to protect our kids from inappropriate content in today’s world. The last place we should have to worry about them is in elementary school. But that’s what happening. Even in a small conservative community like DeWitt, Michigan, educators have forgotten the boundaries. First graders, who have no conceivable way of grasping these manufactured “genders,” are being taught from a book called, “ _They She He Me: Free to Be!_ ,” which suggests, **“You can change pronouns from he to she or she to he. You can use new ones like ze or create your own like tree! Some people use they, which is a perfect way. There are many more pronouns waiting to be discovered and used.”**
---
[_ _ Donate _ _](https://a1e0.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=6626b40fd59aea161b0f8090&u=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.winred.com%2Ftom-barrett-for-congress%2Flet-kids-be-kids&w=618846223a022e7ecb41d30c&c=b_66269bffc16c0c394cf826d3&l=en-US&s=0nEODOujPJ20P6zKk7BIT1DCgps%3D)
---
Parents like us, from throughout the district and Mid-Michigan, made our voices heard. Not long after I talked about his disturbing discovery to Fox News Digital, the school district reversed itself and abandoned the proposal.
---
---
|
---
Peter Willis, I am running for Congress because of our four small kids. I want to make sure we leave the world for them better than we found it. But if we have to fight our own schools to keep our kids safe from inappropriate content, we are already losing the fight.You can count on me to stand up for your kids in Congress, just as I stood up for the kids at Shavey Road Elementary. body:
Support VA UWD members as they host our Immigrant Day of Resilience IG live! ✨ | | | Hi Peter, how did you celebrate Immigrant Day of Resilience on April 15? On Immigrant Day of Resilience, we embrace the care and abundance that enriches our community’s lives. As we recall the ancestors and elders who planted the seeds in our fight for liberation, we envision the just, multi-racial society we’re building together. We kicked off our Immigrant Day of Resilience celebration by spreading care, kinship, and ancestral joy online and straight to your mailbox! We partnered with young BIPOC artists who illustrated three postcards that honor our ancestors who fought for racial justice and democracy. Who are you sharing this artwork with? **📬[In case you missed it, there’s still time to join us in celebrating — order your FREE set of postcards today!](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.v2UrIOJHHKkg0Pk-aGvhyzCKAdQv6ANAIbZ_2K5v_dBk1RrzI-5_J2KTNbkr2UpFdQbIvg5lSUqom2wudACGAroJ6aw7S1ICqg4gL9EQ7J2-Fi-pvmyCy0pbwOw3nM6T05D4RLueYjHPkPFokSvYfnPX-RFqc2L-Rtb8t0z1kmtex8l36MI79ZQJD5WX3vAV1Ps2qlQMAHaaLw6R89V6N8x16mZt25TazA6BrJDah2D8kdXhH882p3cTnOxWMoNp3BJv0c0LUEZ51euQVIjaAh20Fz4HY6gMbZbN71hAWvV1w6bH9aH7XPgqg9DxUYphzHRJ9IqsmpksuM4Vy_BOAZMsB3iuNQ1cJBkyN9xUXUU/45q/7IgnB0DcQFKM2HWLqC4ZqQ/h0/h001.fd2tLulMpF8PBtuFrltTv0TPle56HAJKXKqycXBh2t0) ** **[📮 Order Your Postcards 📮](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.v2UrIOJHHKkg0Pk-aGvhyzCKAdQv6ANAIbZ_2K5v_dBk1RrzI-5_J2KTNbkr2UpFdQbIvg5lSUqom2wudACGAroJ6aw7S1ICqg4gL9EQ7J0-bFK4odr1-sYV_v27fS4bxfm4CBq5K_Wn3auh88LeqBw76rflpobx-2z4N6VUJlQsAPAvQp6IDk-HBEIggxrGkdKqju01I1cc11bp3-158C8RTMyCGHLjW7Roe2mHzFMRLmGHiiYJtSmBsX-vZ5M2Y90U1AvqURyxcGdkYOfqkOWhH0qQLvRW6n0D3lyjdhuYyPDFIReVLKJryae-OCooEp-XcNab02T7UQELHm0gse9AD4nqMbn7fJce1lt817w/45q/7IgnB0DcQFKM2HWLqC4ZqQ/h1/h001.1-2mW3fwxWtWtppGCk7-X8AO8HY3XIj31vHaGgfIndU)[](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.v2UrIOJHHKkg0Pk-aGvhyzCKAdQv6ANAIbZ_2K5v_dBk1RrzI-5_J2KTNbkr2UpFdQbIvg5lSUqom2wudACGAroJ6aw7S1ICqg4gL9EQ7J2SChbgYbOypIgjAXRN12TSrgcRl4UuLh2dTMlVLJkyQ30LeHMxEgXxozqkailNjmaSeZ2YmKv6vxgTEjcdxIc-Yb-P0qmB8CBq-vKxGo3aS6hn4Wd-YnJ0rbiAnISjWPRAocopYh5UhaX1ftCGwkslviimyBg8W1ipREBmc5nJUoHnZYUt0LGh1NWgr2c6KniyA2BLqFL1XFPqzEE_Ilz3NVgIqdCwUTgMMmJT3C3N-zWOU9l3tgUQ76wCjoBj6v0/45q/7IgnB0DcQFKM2HWLqC4ZqQ/h2/h001.zRTdye0B5b48p1I6J00KXK8lwGk5fE9F-8ByeL41FKY)** **Peter, we are our ancestors: we are their resilience, their hope, their joy. When my dad was five years old, he immigrated from Mexico to Texas. He picked cotton and tomatoes in the fields of the Rio Grande Valley, all the while dreaming that one day he would work his way out of poverty and make it to the middle class.
My parents taught me the value of hard work. And I grew up believing that if we worked hard anything was possible.
But when I got to college, I realized my parents didn’t have the money to pay for my tuition _and_ their groceries. So I worked all kinds of odd jobs to put myself through school. It took seven years, but I finished my degree and became the first person in my family to graduate from college.
That got me thinking: **How could it be this difficult, when we did everything right?** And I know that’s a question on the minds of so many families today across Oregon and our nation.
So many people are working so hard and still struggling. They’re doing everything right, but the cost of housing is too high, the burden of student loan debt is too crushing, and the expense of just one health emergency is so extreme that getting ahead is next to impossible.
**Washington needs to do more to help, and I’m working every day to deliver progress. But right now the House is being run by far-right extremists who are, quite frankly, willing to purposefully tank our economy if it means their party can get ahead.**
Instead of making life easier for working families, they’re trying to roll back progress on everything from the environment to LGBTQ+ rights to reproductive freedom. To deliver the kind of leadership our nation deserves — the kind of relief working families are counting on — we need to retake our House majority. And it starts with winning right here in Oregon.
[_**This battleground district could decide which party controls Congress, and it’s going to be one of the most competitive races in the entire country. Will you stand with me today and help make sure we have the resources to win what will be a _very_ tough election?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83521778/468651301/-554069173?refcode=email_041924_Bio&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmNDc1YmZhZS1kZDAwLWVmMTEtYWFmMC03YzFlNTIwMTcwMzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=V8twOWnkXof0y_E26WJXtx0DXqterhDlgkeHoWfXFpM=)

name: Debbie Mucarsel-Powell
subject: The future of our paradise is on the line.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Debbie for Florida
body:
Red Tide Rick has left Florida's future on the line.
| | |
---
This Earth Day, friend, I'm reminded of why I decided to run for Senate in the first place.**[In a lot of ways, this campaign is a love letter to Florida](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83521982/468651824/1820369458?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1108-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS8xMDc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjc3NGIzMDktZGUwMC1lZjExLWFhZjAtN2MxZTUyMDE3MDM4IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=n68X4MS1_iCgjlW9vXEkbLfh8-_yKMoPiqg6qB9iEQ4=) **— so I hope you'll allow me to explain why.
I remember the first time I came to Florida: Having been homesick for the warmth and greenery of Ecuador, my older sister invited me to visit her in Miami, knowing that it might be the cure. _She couldn't have been more right**.**_
Stepping onto the tarmac was like stepping into paradise. Sunny, lush, and all so beautifully green — like so many others, I was instantly smitten by _ Florida. _**So as soon as I could, I packed my things and drove cross-country to make my home in paradise, too.**
In the years since, I've had the privilege to not only build a beautiful life in the Sunshine State — I've dedicated my career to serving it, too.
**And in the face of man-made climate change, and the politicians who willfully turn a blind eye as it destroys the natural beauty that brought me and so many others here, I had to make saving that beauty a key priority.**
In Congress, I fought tirelessly to bolster the natural resilience of our delicate Everglades and wetlands from careless, profit-driven overdevelopment. I fought to fortify our world-class sandy beaches and clear blue waters, safeguard the stunning coral reefs extending along the Keys (the only living barrier reefs in the continental U.S.), and conserve the countless precious species that make Florida one of the most biodiverse states in the country.
**But whether or not Republicans like Rick Scott believe in climate change,
its effects on our homes, our economy, and our future are undeniable.**
Our Sunshine State is on the front lines of a veritable climate crisis. We've long felt the deadly impacts of stronger storms, hotter summers, and rising seas. **And due to our unique vulnerability working families must bear the brunt of sky-rocketing property insurance premiums, while their taxes are spent rebuilding in the wake of the billion-dollar natural disasters we withstand each year, instead of used on the solutions necessary to prevent them.**
But as governor, my opponent banned the use of the term “climate change” and still dismisses it as _"nuisance flooding_ " — **a convenient way to gloss over the fact that his policies were directly responsible for the devastating impacts of those floods on our communities.**
"Red Tide Rick" rolled back the critical environmental protections that could've prevented the toxic algae blooms that led to massive marine animal die-offs and the poisoning of our seafood. His obsession with short-term profit has led to the destruction of not only Florida's beauty but also the robust industries and communities that depend on it to thrive.
In short, Rick Scott has left our state's future on the line — **that's why this Earth Day, I'm counting on you to join me in the fight for Florida and for every community and creature that calls the Sunshine State home.**
[**So friend, if you love our slice of paradise as much as I do, will you donate $5 (or anything you can spare) to help me defeat Rick Scott and his destructive, climate-denying agenda? I know the tides are turning blue, but they'll only stay that way if I can count on grassroots supporters like you with me in the fight for Florida's livable future.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83521983/468651825/1820369458?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1108-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS8xMDc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjc3NGIzMDktZGUwMC1lZjExLWFhZjAtN2MxZTUyMDE3MDM4IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=n68X4MS1_iCgjlW9vXEkbLfh8-_yKMoPiqg6qB9iEQ4=)

clean_body: Red Tide Rick has left Florida's future on the line. | | | This Earth Day, friend, I'm reminded of why I decided to run for Senate in the first place.= — so I hope you'll allow me to explain why. I remember the first time I came to Florida: Having been homesick for the warmth and greenery of Ecuador, my older sister invited me to visit her in Miami, knowing that it might be the cure. She couldn't have been more right. Stepping onto the tarmac was like stepping into paradise. Sunny, lush, and all so beautifully green — like so many others, I was instantly smitten by Florida. So as soon as I could, I packed my things and drove cross-country to make my home in paradise, too. In the years since, I've had the privilege to not only build a beautiful life in the Sunshine State — I've dedicated my career to serving it, too. And in the face of man-made climate change, and the politicians who willfully turn a blind eye as it destroys the natural beauty that brought me and so many others here, I had to make saving that beauty a key priority. In Congress, I fought tirelessly to bolster the natural resilience of our delicate Everglades and wetlands from careless, profit-driven overdevelopment. I fought to fortify our world-class sandy beaches and clear blue waters, safeguard the stunning coral reefs extending along the Keys (the only living barrier reefs in the continental U.S.), and conserve the countless precious species that make Florida one of the most biodiverse states in the country. But whether or not Republicans like Rick Scott believe in climate change, its effects on our homes, our economy, and our future are undeniable. Our Sunshine State is on the front lines of a veritable climate crisis. We've long felt the deadly impacts of stronger storms, hotter summers, and rising seas. And due to our unique vulnerability working families must bear the brunt of sky-rocketing property insurance premiums, while their taxes are spent rebuilding in the wake of the billion-dollar natural disasters we withstand each year, instead of used on the solutions necessary to prevent them. But as governor, my opponent banned the use of the term “climate change” and still dismisses it as "nuisance flooding " — a convenient way to gloss over the fact that his policies were directly responsible for the devastating impacts of those floods on our communities. "Red Tide Rick" rolled back the critical environmental protections that could've prevented the toxic algae blooms that led to massive marine animal die-offs and the poisoning of our seafood. His obsession with short-term profit has led to the destruction of not only Florida's beauty but also the robust industries and communities that depend on it to thrive. Saving our planet is not a question of ability but one of will and values – and I’m running for Congress to be a climate and conservation champion on Day One.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83522329/468653070/-1503676179?refcode=BLU_EM_HFFC_2024-04-22_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDA1NzQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiY2NjMzZlZTEtZGUwMC1lZjExLWFhZjAtN2MxZTUyMDE3MDM4IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=CnL9gkquiXMNpBB--8O20WOaOchy2EQGtU1qDaTc2GE=)

| It's a beautiful Earth Day, Peter.

As a small child, I fell in love with the forests, farms, and waters we are so blessed to have here in Washington. It was this love that led me to become an environmental attorney, fighting to protect these same forests, farms, and waters. Because once lost, we can never get them back again.

As we celebrate Earth Day, it's a powerful reminder of the responsibility we all share to protect our environment for future generations. Our Earth may seem vast, but its resources are finite, and it's up to us to ensure they're preserved for our children and grandchildren.

As Commissioner of Public Lands, I've witnessed firsthand the impacts of climate change on communities in Washington's 6th Congressional District. From devastating wildfires and increasing floods to sea level rise and drought, the challenges we face are real and urgent. _**That’s why I’ve worked to revolutionize our state’s wildfire response, restore 600,000 acres of forests, conserve thousands of acres of forests and farmlands, restore thousands of miles of fish and wildlife habitat, and expand clean energy on our public lands.**_

Saving our planet is not a question of ability but one of will and values – and I’m running for Congress to be a climate and conservation champion on Day One. I’ll continue to be a staunch advocate for addressing the everyday costs of climate change while creating good-paying jobs, protecting vulnerable communities disproportionately affected by environmental hazards, and safeguarding the beauty of the Evergreen State for all of us.

This work is the key to a beautiful, green future for us all. As we celebrate Earth Day and recommit ourselves to that mission, I hope you'll join me.

Gratefully,

Hilary Franz

body:
#
Happy Earth Day! I hope you will take some time today to get outside and celebrate our beautiful planet!
Earth Day not only honors the progress the environmental movement has made over the past 5 decades but is our opportunity to continue raising awareness of the need to protect our planet for future generations.
It’s no secret that the threat of climate change is ever-growing. Scientists agree that global temperatures are rising because of human activity.
Across the world, many communities are experiencing the effects of climate change. We’ve seen it here in the U.S. — violent tropical storms, heatwaves, wildfires, and flooding.
It's crystal clear: We need urgent action on climate change at the federal level now.
So today — on Earth Day — I am asking you to stand with me and send a clear message about where you stand on this issue.
[**Add your name to tell Congress to pass bold legislation to address the climate crisis. We simply cannot afford to wait any longer to save our planet from the disastrous effects of climate change.**](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/signup/em240422_earth_day?source=em240422-1-tt&refcode2=5281.196590.RYWV_C&t=1&akid=5281%2E196590%2ERYWV_C)

Taking action on climate change is about protecting our planet for generations to come. But it is also an opportunity for innovation and to boost our economy — putting millions of people back to work in jobs that pay a living wage.
But taking on the climate crisis is going to require all of us, which is why it's so important that we show we're in this together.
[**Add your name if you agree Congress must take urgent action on climate change.**](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/signup/em240422_earth_day?source=em240422-1-tt&refcode2=5281.196590.RYWV_C&t=3&akid=5281%2E196590%2ERYWV_C)

Mandela

subject: Happy Earth Day!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Wilson for Wisconsin
body:
We need to step up for our planet

| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83522557/468653996/-112884332?refcode=wrpr_hdr&ms=240422_ew_earthday&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDkwMDAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOGNiZDE5NGItZGYwMC1lZjExLWFhZjAtN2MxZTUyMDE3MDM4IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=N2jD3J-Oe_ypXLkW-ovt2lIQg0CvRDmjbkSbwPyfKXE=)

Happy Earth Day, Peter! Earth Day is a day to emphasize environmental protection, something we need now more than ever as we face the climate crisis. So much of how we live is at stake if we don’t act to save our planet. One element that is critically important here in WI-03: family farms. subject: Earth Day Must Be Every Day
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Rick Coplen

Pennsylvanians don’t need to look far to see the effects of climate change on our lives.

Farmers are seeing changes in the growing season. Crop yields are expected to fall. Droughts and floods result from more frequent extreme weather events. The electric grid is straining under increased demand for cooling.

**I believe that, together, we can slow, halt and reverse climate change. But not with climate deniers like Scott Perry misrepresenting us.**

Reasonable people agree on two things:
1. Climate change poses a very real, very immediate threat.
2. Climate change deniers are only making matters worse.

President Biden and Democrats in Congress have made historic progress by investing in climate action – progress that I believe we can take even further so that the U.S. becomes a true leader in the global effort against climate change.

Scott Perry voted to repeal key climate initiatives as part of the GOP’s partisan debt ceiling fiasco and has repeatedly voted to subsidize Big Oil with $20 billion of taxpayers’ hard-earned money.

The League of Conservation Voters gave Perry a 0% on his 2022 National Environment Scorecard. I don’t think that terrible rating is changing any time soon.

I’m running for Congress because Scott Perry is leaving Pennsylvania behind in creating a clean energy future that addresses climate change, provides good-paying jobs, and lowers costs for our families and businesses.

**Climate change is real, and it will not solve itself. As individuals, communities, and national governments we must help by committing to:**
* Achieve global carbon neutrality by 2050.
* Achieve 100% renewable energy by accelerating the development and deployment of wind, solar, nuclear fusion, and geothermal energy.
* Fulfill the climate goals expressed in the Paris Climate Agreement.

I look forward to celebrating Earth Day in Congress, not just on April 22 but every day I serve.

– Rick

clean_body: | Pennsylvanians don’t need to look far to see the effects of climate change on our lives. Farmers are seeing changes in the growing season. Crop yields are expected to fall. Droughts and floods result from more frequent extreme weather events. The electric grid is straining under increased demand for cooling. I believe that, together, we can slow, halt and reverse climate change. But not with climate deniers like Scott Perry misrepresenting us. Reasonable people agree on two things: 1. Climate change poses a very real, very immediate threat. 2. Climate change deniers are only making matters worse. President Biden and Democrats in Congress have made historic progress by investing in climate action – progress that I believe we can take even further so that the U.S. becomes a true leader in the global effort against climate change. Scott Perry voted to repeal key climate initiatives as part of the GOP’s partisan debt ceiling fiasco and has repeatedly voted to subsidize Big Oil with $20 billion of taxpayers’ hard-earned money. The League of Conservation Voters gave Perry a 0% on his 2022 National Environment Scorecard. I don’t think that terrible rating is changing any time soon. I’m running for Congress because Scott Perry is leaving Pennsylvania behind in creating a clean energy future that addresses climate change, provides good-paying jobs, and lowers costs for our families and businesses. Climate change is real, and it will not solve itself. As individuals, communities, and national governments we must help by committing to: Achieve global carbon neutrality by 2050. Achieve 100% renewable energy by accelerating the development and deployment of wind, solar, nuclear fusion, and geothermal energy. Fulfill the climate goals expressed in the Paris Climate Agreement. I look forward to celebrating Earth Day in Congress, not just on April 22 but every day I serve. – Rick | | =** | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|--- Paid for by Friends of Rick Coplen | =

Friends,
Tomorrow is Primary Election Day! Polls will be open Tuesday, April 23rd from 7:00 A.M. to 8:00 P.M.
I am asking you to spread the word and get all your friends and family to vote!
I have said this over and over on the campaign trail...”we are losing our country.” And we are! We are losing our country to the radical left that has pushed endless foreign funding without securing our border, high taxes, high gas prices, a woke agenda in schools and sports, out-of-control spending, and more. Unfortunately, some “Republicans” are going along with these terrible policies and putting America Last!
That is why I am running - because it is time we defeat the uniparty, take our country back, and start focusing on doing what is best for the American people! That is what America First is all about.
I am running on my proven conservative record in the state House. I am also running as a proven electoral winner - something neither of my opponents has ever had any success at despite their numerous attempts to get into elected office.
Tomorrow, with your help, we will be successful again and we can then take the fight directly to Susan Wild! I appreciate all the help and support we have received throughout the campaign. It is truly humbling.
Now, one last request for the Primary and our campaign to turn PA-7 RED: If you can please take five minutes out of your busy day to text 10 friends and family members as one last push to get them to vote for me (Ryan Mackenzie) and that I would be honored to have their vote.

Ryan Mackenzie

Happy Earth Day, Peter!

Every Earth Day, we are reminded of the incredible nature that surrounds us here in our district. From Lake Sammamish to the Wenatchee Valley, our district has beauty like no other. Yet today is also a stark reminder of how our changing climate affects the lands we hold dear.

Over the past few years, we’ve seen destructive wildfires become all too common, new diseases affecting crops and trees like never before, and warmer temperatures bringing drastic changes to our tributaries and causing species extinction. **It’s clear: climate change is one of the greatest threats of our time.**

Kim knows the dangers of climate change, and she’s used her voice in Congress to advocate for legislation that will address the needs of our environment. In fact, she helped pass the bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act which included provisions to make our forests more resilient to wildfires, protect our rivers and streams, and more. She has advocated for the permanent reauthorization of the Land and Water Conservation Fund and has cosponsored legislation that would ensure a safe and secure water supply for Central Washington during drought years. **But she knows there’s still more work to be done.**

body:
# [#] Hi folks,

Tonight marks the first night of Passover, one of the most important holidays for those of us in the Jewish community. We commemorate the Exodus of the Israelites from Egypt. On this holiday, we take a pause to think of those around the world suffering from bondage and oppression.

This night is different from all other nights, as we gather with friends and family to tell the Passover story by reading the Haggadah at our seders. I look forward to this beautiful tradition each year, for the opportunity to see loved ones and remember this ancient story of liberation that has inspired our people for thousands of years.

If you’re celebrating Passover this year, I hope you have a wonderful seder.

Chag Kasher V’Sameach,

Josh

body:
Don't miss the latest news on the Ohio election integrity lawsuit! | | | [ ](https://gfiohio.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c2cee5a5358289d5dd20ff17d&id=2106ead456&e=5c740fa3e2)
---
| This week's 3 most important things you need to know or actions you need to take to help us recapture our cities, state, and nation.

Thank you for subscribing & staying subscribed!
---
| | | **
OHIO ELECTION INTEGRITY!
LAWSUIT! • LITIGATION!
OHIOANS FIGHTING BACK!
THEY NEED OUR HELP!**

---
|
Help protect civil rights and Ohio's elections by donating to the [**United Sovereign Americans**](https://gfiohio.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c2cee5a5358289d5dd20ff17d&id=869b2d7949&e=5c740fa3e2) (USA) lawsuit. USA, a grassroots group active in 27 states, uses voter roll analyses to initiate lawsuits safeguarding election integrity and civil rights, referencing federal laws and the US Constitution. In Ohio, significant voter roll discrepancies have been identified, necessitating immediate legal action to ensure fair elections. USA volunteers have identified many suspected anomalies in our voter rolls including:
* 1,046,431 ineligible or uncertain registration violations within the Ohio State voter roll database.
* 602,631 votes cast by ineligible or uncertain registrants.
* 1,162,079 more votes counted than voters who voted in the 2022 general election at the time of certification. No one knows who cast them.
* 713,262 apparent voting violations in excess of the legal standard of system accuracy for a valid federal election. Maximum allowable system errors for the 2022 general election in Ohio was 34.
* Certification, as defined by law, an attestation of accuracy and compliance, appears to have been fraudulent and illegal.

With the 2024 elections approaching, USA aims to file in 10 federal courts and needs $50,000 to launch the Ohio lawsuit. Economic challenges persist, but your support is crucial. Please donate generously to this critical initiative by clicking [**HERE**](https://gfiohio.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c2cee5a5358289d5dd20ff17d&id=9026cebbeb&e=5c740fa3e2) or on the image below.

Thank you!

---
| [](https://gfiohio.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c2cee5a5358289d5dd20ff17d&id=0ad34b9515&e=5c740fa3e2)
---
| |
**OHIO PARENTS ALERT!
FIX OUR PUBLIC SCHOOLS!
BECOME A BOARD MEMBER!
HERE'S HOW!**

---
|
Next year, in November of 2025, all public school districts in Ohio will have at least 2 school board seats up for re-election, or if there is no incumbent for the seat, up for election.

We need concerned citizens who are for parental rights, a return to the basics of education, and completely depoliticizing Ohio's public schools, to run for these school board seats.

Anyone can run & there is no need for any kind of special qualifications, experience, or skills. All that's needed is a desire & common sense.

And, the Ohio School Board Constitutional Coalition (OSBCC) can help you every step of the way. 40% of the candidates they helped last election won!

If you are interested, or know someone who is, please, please, please make sure you (or they) visit the OSBCC website & register to start getting OSBCC's regular emails & training notices [**HERE**](https://gfiohio.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c2cee5a5358289d5dd20ff17d&id=d24142a1ad&e=5c740fa3e2) or by clicking on the image below

If you (or they) are anxious to start preparing to run for a school board seat, go to (or have them go to) the contact page & send OSBCC an email or fill out the contact form [**HERE**](https://gfiohio.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c2cee5a5358289d5dd20ff17d&id=6df00a4821&e=5c740fa3e2). The volunteers at OSBCC will get back to you to get you started off strong. It's not too early to start your campaign!

THANK YOU!

---
| [ ](https://gfiohio.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c2cee5a5358289d5dd20ff17d&id=258d52bc49&e=5c740fa3e2)
---
|
---
| |
**CONVENIENT TEXT (SMS)
"SHORT CODE" KEYWORDS
HELP FREEDOM GROW!**

---
|
Phone text (SMS) short-code keywords are specific words or phrases assigned to a short numeric code, typically five or six digits, used for sending and receiving text messages, especially in marketing and customer service. When users text a keyword to a designated short code, they can subscribe to services, participate in promotions, or request information. The system automatically processes these messages based on the keyword. For example, texting "JOIN" to a certain number might subscribe a user to a promotional newsletter.

The Grassroots Freedom Initiative (GFI) has implemented several text short-code keywords for your use, and we’ll likely be adding many more over time. They are:

**1) GFI**
Text “GFI” to 66866 and follow the prompts to add an email directly into our mailing list to receive emails like this one you are reading!
_* If you are already subscribed & receiving this email, please refrain from sending this keyword. *_

**2) LIST**
Text “LIST” to 66866 and follow the prompts to be sent a list of the most important grassroots websites and organizations that you need to be a part of!

**3) X**
Are you an X (formerly known as Twitter) user? If so, text “X” to 66866 and follow the prompts to join our "Community" on X! It's called "The Ohio X Brigade". Don't know what an X Community is? Don't worry, we'll help you out!

Use these keywords and short-code with your friends and neighbors to get them introduced to self-governance activism in Ohio! Thank you (and them!) for joining us!

Peter,

We must come to grips with the reality that we will continue to feel the effects of climate change across all sectors of our life.

In Missouri, we're already feeling the impacts of climate change on our way of life and the safety of vulnerable communities. That’s why I've made it a priority on this campaign to engage with advocacy groups to better understand the challenges our St. Louis faces.

I’m committed to working alongside these groups to ensure the removal and cleanup of radioactive waste near Westlake Landfill and along Coldwater Creek in North St. Louis County. **And as your representative, I'll continue to fight for policies that prioritize environmental justice and promote renewable energy to make a difference for our planet and future generations.**

But addressing climate change isn't just about cleaning up past mistakes — it's about building a sustainable future, ensuring future generations of St. Louisans will get to experience the beauty and benefits of our natural environment just as we did.
